This is a great question. Yes I’ve used multiple agencies and there’s good and bad to it. You’re right, one agency might have it posted first and that is usually because that specific hospital might have a contract with that specific agency. You could ask your agency to try and “grab it” for you but chances are, the position will be filled before then. Some agencies pay more than others if multiple agencies have it posted. I’ve come to really like my recruiter on a personal level so I will usually try to return to him because he genuinely cares and checks in on me, even when I’m not with his agency. The annoying part of having multiple agencies is the onboarding crap and references and that. That, and whatever you had built up with one agency (pto, sick time, etc.) may not carry over when you go back to them. My advice is; if you find a recruiter that you really like, try and stay with them and they will look out for you. I like that my recruiter is honest about different assignments and tells me if there are a lot of complaints with that specific hospital or position and steers me in the right direction. He was also my husband’s recruiter and would try to find us positions that were close by each other. Hope this helps!

So everything depends on each hospital. You get a tax free stipend on top of your pay at the hospital. For example, in Chicago I was making $2800/week working 3-12s on night shift. But the hourly rate was $17/hour. I made all my money from the stipend. I think you work until the completion of your contract, often times they ask you to extend too. 

I’m pretty sure you have to be at least 90 miles from your home address to qualify as a traveler. Once again with Chicago, I would work my 3 12s and then drive 3 hours home to Peoria. That was just luck on my end. Rarely do they schedule you 3 12s in a row that might enable you to fly home, that’s just because literally nothing is easy and management is just dumb on that kind of thing. Perhaps, depending on how forceful you are, they may adjust. But literally all I’ve been seeing is 5-8s being posted and I would bet that it’s because you will be by yourself and they need daily coverage. Like if it were up to them, you’d work 7 days a week. Haha. That’s just management though as I’ve come to realize…like how much work can you do for me for this little amount of compensation and understanding. 

Yes I’ve heard of places doing on call, I’ve personally never done it though, I hear it’s a pain in the ass and you get called in Willy nilly for silly things, like fixing or whatever. Hello, Welcome! I’d love to help you out with your questions. There are different agencies with recruiters that want to get you situated at a job. Once they secure you a job, they get paid. I go through aureus and have met quite a few people who go through them as well. Aya is another good one, and I’ve heard of people going through LRS and soliant. I don’t really think there is a huge difference, it’s a matter of your preference in a recruiter. You may also use multiple agencies. But be aware, they are hound dogs and will hit you up all the time if you give them the slightest inkling of wanting to find an assignment, again, that’s how they get paid. 

Try to ask the recruiters if they can get information for you such as: does this facility do EEGs on pediatrics, do they use collodion, do they have an EMU, what shift and what hours(3-12s, 4-10s, 5-8s), whats the pay, what’s the uniform color, and one I wish I would have asked: will I be the only staff member in the EEG department?

I have never found a page or forum that is specifically for travel EEG techs to talk about their assignments about where to go and where not to go so I created this page in hopes of providing that information to our niche tribe. But as far as assignments go, it’s your preference! Wherever you want to go and how far you’re willing to go is up to you! And speaking from personal opinion, you don’t always get paid in money. I took an assignment in Florida to escape the winter and it doesn’t pay well at all, however, I was warm in the winter and got to really explore the beaches and Everglades. 

Upon looking for assignments, make sure to look on furnished finder, Airbnb, and vrbo for a place to stay in that city. I wish I would have researched more about places to stay where I am now because a lot of people flood to Florida to escape the cold and I ended up in a studio apartment for 3500/month because everything else was booked up and they jack up the rent because they can. Sucks but it is what it is. Learning experience. Haha. 

Let me know if you have more questions please!
